claim: A static triangular-mesh closest-point representation of signed distance, local surface normal, curvature, and optional surface coordinates can define integrable geometry-dependent impedance coordinates and a conditionally passive impedance law; in one silicone-phantom robot experiment, negative desired distance maintained nearly continuous contact without the loss-of-contact/impact behavior reported for two feed-forward-force baselines. This supports local surface geometry as control-relevant mechanism evidence, but it does not establish the decision value or minimal sufficiency of nested soft-contact state because mesh geometry is not independent contact-area sensing and the study did not measure tangential wrench capacity or contact history, test held-out continuous material/geometry shifts or impedance-action equivalence, or evaluate ultrasound image quality.
claim_locator: Abstract/contribution; theory/mechanism; discrete geometry; experiment; authors' limitations/future work (Controller-supplied admitted full-text dossier; PDF page numbers were not preserved in the dossier and are therefore not fabricated)
problem_and_setting: The bound problem P-SOFTSCAN-STATE-01 v1 asks whether independent contact area, local geometry, tangential force/moment, and history have decision value for impedance selection under held-out continuous soft-contact shifts, and what representation is minimally sufficient relative to simpler or model-agnostic feedback. This paper instead studies geometry-dependent impedance control for robotic ultrasound-like scanning over a known arbitrary surface, using a 7-DoF DLR MIRO, a dummy spherical-tip tool, and a static triangular mesh of a Dragon Skin silicone phantom with Shore 10A hardness, an approximately 1 cm wall, and solid backing.
method_or_mechanism: The controller forms task coordinates from signed distance to a closest-point surface proxy and tool alignment to the proxy normal, with an optional surface parametrization. Its Jacobian uses the normal, shape operator or principal curvature, and orientation terms. Positive-definite stiffness and damping applied to integrable coordinates are stated by the authors to yield a passive impedance law. On a triangular mesh, an AABB tree finds the closest triangle/proxy point; barycentric interpolation supplies normals, curvatures, and parameter values; quadric fitting supplies principal curvature information; and ARAP supplies an approximately isometric two-dimensional parametrization for disk-topology surfaces. A negative desired signed distance produces passive contact force and limits commanded penetration. The passivity statement is conditional theory based on coordinate integrability, gains, and the valid nearest-point region; the robot experiment is empirical behavior in one setup and is not experimental proof of passivity.
content_summary: The paper reports real-time mesh-based task and Jacobian evaluation in a 3 kHz control loop and trajectory tracking on a silicone phantom. Lissajous tracking RMSE was 0.917 mm for s1, 1.465 mm for s2, and 0.871 mm for positive desired distance. For the same path, mean plus or minus standard-deviation Fz was -2.178 plus or minus 0.521 N for Cartesian impedance with -2 N feed-forward, -2.183 plus or minus 0.495 N for mesh impedance with -2 N feed-forward, and -2.403 plus or minus 0.498 N for mesh impedance with desired distance -10 mm and kd 250 N/m. The authors report loss of contact followed by impact for both feed-forward strategies and nearly continuous contact without that impact for negative-distance mesh impedance. The study uses a preoperative/static surface representation and does not evaluate human tissue, an ultrasound imaging endpoint, held-out shifts, independent contact area, tangential wrench capacity, or viscoelastic history.
synthesis_role: Indirect mechanism evidence for CHAIN-SPATIAL-SUFFICIENCY and CHAIN-CLOSED-LOOP-ABSORPTION, and boundary-setting evidence for OBL-SPATIAL-OBSERVABILITY and OBL-INDEPENDENT-ENDPOINT. It shows that local mesh-derived normal and curvature can enter an integrable spatial controller and that feedback through signed-distance impedance can absorb some contact-maintenance demands in one fixed setting. It does not satisfy spatial observability for independent finite contact area, and it leaves the independent scanning-task endpoint unmet because no diagnostic ultrasound image quality was measured. It supplies no affirmative evidence for CHAIN-TANGENTIAL-SUFFICIENCY or CHAIN-HISTORY-SUFFICIENCY.
development_link: The useful design implication is to include a static-geometry baseline using closest-point signed distance, local normal, and curvature, together with a simpler negative-distance impedance policy. The residual delta is a direct nested-representation decision test: add independent contact-area, tangential wrench, and history channels one level at a time; compare policies under held-out continuous material and geometry shifts while controlling for impedance-action equivalence; measure force/wrench safety plus an independent ultrasound scanning endpoint; and retain the disconfirming outcome that the mesh/signed-distance or model-agnostic baseline is sufficient. This paper cannot determine the minimal sufficient representation or whether richer contact state has incremental decision value.

evidence.locator: Theory/mechanism: parallel-surface construction and task coordinates (Controller-supplied dossier; PDF page number unavailable)
evidence.finding: The nearest-point parallel-surface map is assumed one-to-one only for absolute signed distance below the minimum curvature radius; within the integrable-coordinate construction, the authors state that positive-definite stiffness and damping yield a passive impedance law. This is a conditional analytical claim, not an experimentally verified passivity certificate for arbitrary deformable contact.

evidence.locator: Discrete geometry: triangular-mesh implementation (Controller-supplied dossier; PDF page number unavailable)
evidence.finding: Closest-triangle search, barycentric interpolation, fitted principal curvatures/directions, and ARAP surface coordinates provide local mesh geometry at runtime. These are properties of the represented surface and proxy map, not measurements of the independent finite contact patch.

evidence.locator: Experiment: Lissajous tracking and three force strategies (Controller-supplied dossier; PDF page number unavailable)
evidence.finding: Negative-distance mesh impedance maintained almost continuous contact without the loss-of-contact/impact behavior observed for the two -2 N feed-forward baselines; reported Fz variability was similar across strategies. This supports contact-maintenance behavior in one silicone-phantom setup but does not isolate passivity, representation minimality, or generalization under held-out shifts.

evidence.locator: Experiment: platform, phantom, and timing (Controller-supplied dossier; PDF page number unavailable)
evidence.finding: The 13,367-vertex and 26,360-face mesh was used at a 3 kHz control rate; AABB initialization took 18 ms and the task/Jacobian call took 11.91 microseconds. This supports real-time feasibility for the reported static-mesh implementation.

evidence.locator: Authors' limitations/future work and experiment scope (Controller-supplied dossier; PDF page number unavailable)
evidence.finding: The authors call for realistic clinical in-vitro validation, clinicians, image-quality visual servoing, local stiffness estimation, and mesh updates for deformable tissue. From the reported measurements, the reader assesses that OBL-INDEPENDENT-ENDPOINT remains unmet because no ultrasound image or diagnostic-quality endpoint was evaluated.

boundary_conditions: The closest-point/parallel-surface mapping is restricted to offsets whose absolute signed distance is below the minimum curvature radius; farther offsets may self-intersect.
The demonstrated surface representation is a known preoperative/static triangular mesh, not an online estimate of a deforming tissue surface or contact patch.
ARAP parametrization is described for disk-topology surfaces and is only approximately isometric.

The experiment used one Dragon Skin silicone phantom with Shore 10A hardness, approximately 1 cm wall thickness, solid backing, and a dummy spherical-tip tool rather than human tissue and an ultrasound probe producing diagnostic images.
Controller gains were selected heuristically from experimental examination and known silicone stiffness; they were not selected or validated across held-out continuous material or geometry shifts.
The negative-distance result compares three strategies on the same path in the reported setup; it does not test nested state additions, policy action equivalence, or representation minimality.
High-curvature regions can generate high joint velocity; the authors identify prediction and limiting of this velocity as future safety work.
assumptions: The reference surface is oriented and has a smooth normal field, and the nearest-point proxy is unique in the operated offset region.
The task coordinates remain integrable, and stiffness and damping matrices are positive definite, for the stated passivity result.
The static mesh, interpolated normal, and fitted curvature adequately represent the physical surface encountered by the tool.
The printed heuristic relation among desired contact force, distance-coordinate stiffness, and object stiffness is adequate for selecting desired penetration in the reported setting.

Unmeasured deformability, local stiffness variation, finite contact area, frictional/tangential capacity, and viscoelastic memory do not invalidate the proxy-control behavior in the demonstrated experiment.

reported: Both -2 N feed-forward-force strategies lost contact and were followed by impact on the reported path, whereas negative-distance mesh impedance maintained almost continuous contact without that impact.
The authors report that realistic clinical in-vitro validation with clinicians is still needed and place ultrasound image-quality visual servoing in future work.

The authors identify deformable-tissue handling through local stiffness estimation and mesh update, out-of-plane rotation, focal-point/self-intersection handling, and arbitrary foliations as unresolved work.
The authors note that high-curvature regions can produce high joint velocity and propose predicting and limiting it for safety.
inferred: The paper cannot determine whether independent contact area, tangential wrench, or history has incremental decision value because those channels were neither measured nor ablated.

The paper cannot establish a minimally sufficient nested contact representation because it compares control strategies rather than controlled representation levels and does not enforce impedance-action equivalence.
The experimental result does not demonstrate robustness to held-out continuous material or geometry shifts because only the reported phantom/setup was evaluated.
The force/contact result cannot substitute for an independent scanning-task endpoint because no ultrasound image quality or diagnostic outcome was measured.

The reported contact-maintenance behavior is consistent with a closed-loop absorption account, but the experiment does not prove that passivity, rather than other controller or setup factors, caused the observed difference.
